reasons: Cited Section 20 meets the preferred position: 20.1 provides an unqualified Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP infringement claims covering Customer, Affiliates and their personnel; 20.2 adds breach of Applicable Law, Customer Data breach caused by Vendor, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, matching model language (a)-(d).

Standard indemnity procedure (prompt notice, cooperation at indemnifying Party's expense, control of defence, prejudice-limited notice failure, settlement consent) is present in 20.4, and 20.5 supplies procure/modify/replace/refund remedies without allowing termination of unaffected Services.

Customer's reverse indemnity in 20.3 is appropriately narrow (unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised; Customer's own violation of law) with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination and Vendor instructions, so the one-way-indemnity walk-away risk is absent.
Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under 21.3, so they sit outside the liability cap — better than the fallback's 3x super-cap; no compromise language is needed.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline was applied and no counterparty comment was raised; deterministic check confirms Vendor IP indemnity is present.
